item.title: How to use Le Chat, now called Mistral Vibe
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Le Chat became Vibe on May 28, 2026. Sign in at chat.mistral.ai or in the iOS or Android app. Your conversations, settings and plan carried over. item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Le Chat, now called Mistral Vibe: a practical guide","dek":"Mistral renamed its Le Chat assistant to Vibe in May 2026. Here is how to sign in, when to use Chat or Work mode, prompts to copy, and what the free plan leaves out.","summary":"Le Chat, Mistral AI's assistant, was renamed Vibe on May 28, 2026, and existing accounts, conversations and plans carried over. Use Chat for quick questions and Work for multi-step tasks, which shows you a plan to approve before it starts.","tags":["Le Chat","Mistral AI","Mistral Vibe","AI assistant","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you are looking up how to use Le Chat, the first thing to know is that it has a new name. On May 28, 2026, Mistral AI renamed Le Chat to Vibe, its single assistant for everyday work and for coding. Mistral's help center says your account, plan, conversations and saved content carried over, and you still sign in with the same login at chat.mistral.ai.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral help center: Le Chat is now Vibe","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/682992-le-chat-is-now-vibe"},{"name":"Mistral AI: Vibe announcement","url":"https://mistral.ai/it/news/vibe-agent/"},{"name":"The Decoder: Mistral rebrands Le Chat as Vibe","url":"https://the-decoder.com/mistral-rebrands-lechat-as-vibe-betting-its-chatbots-future-is-as-a-full-blown-work-agent/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Le Chat first launched in February 2024, and iOS and Android apps followed in February 2025. Mistral describes it as a multilingual assistant that can search the web, generate images, write and debug code, summarize documents or simply talk. The help center says it chooses its tools based on what you ask, so you do not have to switch them on for each question.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral help center: What is Le Chat and how do I use it","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347453-what-is-le-chat-and-how-do-i-use-it"},{"name":"Wikipedia: Mistral Vibe","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_Vibe"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Le Chat in its new Vibe form","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Sign in at chat.mistral.ai or in the app","text":"Open chat.mistral.ai in a browser, or install the app from the App Store or Google Play. If you had a Le Chat account, use the same login and your old conversations are there. Mistral's help center notes that some features need you to be logged in, so create an account even if you only plan to use the free plan.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose Chat or Work","text":"Vibe has three modes. Chat is the turn by turn conversation Le Chat was known for. Work is for tasks with several steps across your apps and files. Code is for developers. In heise's hands on test, logged in free users switched between Chat and Work with a control in the top left corner of the start screen. Mistral's announcement says Chat mode will be retired, with Le Chat history staying available in Work mode.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write the full task, not a keyword","text":"Mistral's help center says the assistant has no prior context about you, so give it specific instructions. Say what you want, what to work from and what the answer should look like. Short keyword queries get generic answers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A news brief with sources","text":"Search the web for news about [topic] from the last 7 days. Give me 5 bullet points, each with one source link. End with one sentence on what to watch next. Leave out anything older than 7 days.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Upload a file and ask about it","text":"Mistral lists document and image understanding among the core features: you upload a file or picture and ask questions about it. For files you want to reuse, Libraries act as personal knowledge bases you can chat with, and Projects group related chats into folders.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Pull the key facts out of a document","text":"Read the attached [contract / report / PDF]. List every date, amount and deadline it mentions in a table with three columns: item, value, page. Then tell me in three sentences what I need to do and by when.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Hand a multi-step job to Work mode","text":"Work mode is where Vibe differs most from the old Le Chat. According to Mistral, it writes a plan and asks for your approval before it starts, works across connected apps such as Google Workspace, Outlook, SharePoint, Slack and GitHub, and streams its progress. You can expand each tool call to see what went in and what came out. Tasks can also run on a schedule: once, daily, weekly or monthly, with a notification when they finish.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A weekly task for Work mode","text":"Every Monday, read the spreadsheet [file name] and compare this week's [sales / signups / expenses] with last week's. Make one chart and a five line summary of what changed, and draft it in a canvas I can send to my team.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Read the plan Work mode shows you before you approve it. It is the cheapest place to catch a wrong file, a wrong inbox or a step you did not ask for.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Features worth knowing","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Mistral's capabilities overview lists Think mode, which uses its reasoning model for harder questions; Voice mode, so you can talk instead of type; Deep Research for multi-step web research; a Code Interpreter that runs Python in a secure environment; Canvas, an editor you work in together with the assistant; and image generation with models from Black Forest Labs. The help center adds that web search can draw on news from AFP and AP.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral help center: What is Le Chat and how do I use it","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347453-what-is-le-chat-and-how-do-i-use-it"},{"name":"Mistral help center: An overview of Le Chat's capabilities","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347531-an-overview-of-le-chat-s-capabilities"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Work mode also has Skills, reusable workflows that Mistral says are built on open standards. In heise's test, skills could be turned on or off one by one, loaded automatically or called by naming them in a prompt, and users could import their own skills written in Markdown. A pre-installed skill-creator helps you build new ones.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral AI: Vibe announcement","url":"https://mistral.ai/it/news/vibe-agent/"},{"name":"heise: Mistral Vibe, trying out the Work and Code interfaces","url":"https://heise.de/-11312502"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Plans and what the free version leaves out","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Mistral's announcement lists four plans: Free for quick answers and simple everyday tasks, Pro at $14.99 a month, Team at $24.99 per user a month with a shared workspace and admin controls, and Enterprise with custom deployments. The help center says the free plan includes most features with daily caps, Pro removes the cap on messages, and a discounted Pro plan exists for eligible students and educators.","sources":[{"name":"Mistral help center: What is Le Chat and how do I use it","url":"https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347453-what-is-le-chat-and-how-do-i-use-it"},{"name":"Mistral AI: Vibe announcement","url":"https://mistral.ai/it/news/vibe-agent/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Exact limits are hard to pin down. heise reported that the free plan cannot create canvases or run remote coding sessions, and that Pro and Team get five times as many web searches and up to 40 times as many image generations as Free, but that Mistral does not publish the underlying numbers. The Decoder also noted that Mistral had not given concrete usage limits for Work mode. heise quoted prices in euros that differ from the dollar prices on Mistral's page, so check the price shown in your own account.","sources":[{"name":"heise: Mistral Vibe, trying out the Work and Code interfaces","url":"https://heise.de/-11312502"},{"name":"The Decoder: Mistral rebrands Le Chat as Vibe","url":"https://the-decoder.com/mistral-rebrands-lechat-as-vibe-betting-its-chatbots-future-is-as-a-full-blown-work-agent/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"On the free plan, the help center says your conversations may be used to train Mistral's models unless you opt out in your account settings. Do that before you paste in anything private.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where it falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The rename makes Vibe harder to learn than Le Chat was. There are now three modes, one of them due to be retired, and the help pages are split between the old help center and Mistral's developer docs. heise also found rough edges in Work mode: a writing skill could not pull information from connected apps on its own, and pre-installed skills could not be changed with the skill-creator.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The practical approach is to start in Chat with one real question you would otherwise search for, then try Work mode on one small, repeatable job, such as a weekly summary from a single spreadsheet. If the plan it writes matches what you would have done yourself, give it a bigger task. If it keeps hitting the free caps, that is the point to decide whether Pro is worth it for you.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Synthesia to make AI avatar videos
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Describe the topic, the audience and the goal, or attach a PDF, slides or a Word file. Pick a length: Auto, Short, Medium or Long. Synthesia drafts the scenes and the script first. Edit, delete or add sections before you build the video. The editor works like slides: scenes on the left, the script at the bottom. Check the pricing page on the day you buy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"When Synthesia is worth it","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Wyzowl, a video production company, rated Synthesia 4.5 out of 5 and praised its speed and cost compared with filming. item.title: How to use Vercel v0 for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in at v0.app, start a chat and describe what you want in plain words. A screenshot, a mockup or a Figma design also works as a starting point. Open the Design tab, select an element and change its style, then click Apply. Save your prompts for layout and behavior. Publish puts the app on a vercel.app address. Connect your own domain later. Reviews say the free plan has about $5 of credits a month. Sources: v0 docs: Quickstart, v0 docs: Introduction, v0 docs: FAQs, NxCode: v0 by Vercel complete guide 2026, Taskade: v0 by Vercel review 2026.

Credits can also go fast: NxCode warns that heavy use of the top model can burn through the free $5 in a single session, and Taskade says heavy users report the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Vercel's own FAQ is plain about limits too. v0 needs an internet connection, the generated code may be incomplete or contain bugs, and you are responsible for checking that it fits your use. The full experience with previews, environment variables and deployments assumes your GitHub repository is connected to a Vercel project, although you can export the code and host it elsewhere.","sources":[{"name":"v0 docs: FAQs","url":"https://v0.app/docs/faqs"},{"name":"NxCode: v0 by Vercel complete guide 2026","url":"https://www.nxcode.io/resources/news/v0-by-vercel-complete-guide-2026"},{"name":"Taskade: v0 by Vercel review 2026","url":"https://www.taskade.com/blog/v0-review"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The practical way to use the free plan is to treat it as a sketchbook. Build one small app end to end, publish it, and learn where v0 needs precise prompts. If you hit the daily or monthly limit before the app works, that is the moment to judge whether a paid plan is worth it for you.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Photoroom for product photos
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Upload a photo in the app or at app.photoroom.com. The background is removed automatically. Shoot on a plain surface in good light for the cleanest edge. Pick a plain white background for marketplaces, or let AI Backgrounds build a styled scene. Add an AI shadow so the product does not look pasted on. Batch mode applies the same edits to many photos at once. Free accounts get 250 exports a month. Paid plans start at $7.50 a month, billed yearly. A Research Report searches, screens and extracts automatically and writes a structured answer, with templates such as General Review, 1-Page Overview and Research Gap Analysis. The Systematic Review is the step by step workflow where you control every stage. The older Find Papers, Extract Data and Chat with Papers tools were replaced by the Research Agent.","sources":[{"name":"Elicit Help Center: Elicit's Research Agent","url":"https://support.elicit.com/en/articles/14756886-elicit-s-research-agent"},{"name":"Elicit Help Center: Research Reports","url":"https://support.elicit.com/en/articles/14756862-get-a-research-report-to-generate-in-depth-answers-automatically-in-elicit"},{"name":"Elicit Help Center: Export your data","url":"https://support.elicit.com/en/articles/14758189-export-your-data-from-elicit"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use a Research Report when you need a fast map of a topic or a list of seed papers. Extract data into columns","text":"Add columns for what you want from each paper, such as sample size, study design or main result. item.title: OpenAI and Cisco built a free AI shield that blocks attacks before Linux servers get patched
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Shirudo, Japanese for shield, runs small eBPF programs inside Linux that block a known exploit while the service keeps running. Teams can watch a shield in test mode first, then deploy it after approval, with no restart. In an OpenAI test, Codex built a shield that stopped a Java4Shell attack on a running Elasticsearch server. Shields are signed and checked before they load. The code is free on GitHub. Sources: OpenAI, SiliconANGLE, The Register.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Shirudo logo on an orange gradient with the OpenAI and Cisco logos along the bottom.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo to shield unpatched Linux systems","dek":"The open-source runtime uses eBPF programs, which Codex can write, to block known exploits on running servers until a patch is installed.","summary":"OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo on November 23, 2026, an open-source runtime that applies temporary protections called shields to running Linux systems. In a controlled test, a shield written by Codex blocked a Java4Shell exploit on a live Elasticsearch service without a restart.","seo_title":"OpenAI and Cisco Shirudo: open-source shield for Linux","seo_description":"OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source eBPF runtime that blocks known exploits on live Linux servers before patches. How it works and the Codex test.","answer_summary":"Shirudo is an open-source runtime from OpenAI and Cisco that uses signed eBPF programs, called shields, to block known exploits on running Linux systems while teams test and install patches.","tags":["OpenAI","Cisco","Shirudo","Codex","Linux","Cybersecurity"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo on November 23, 2026, an open-source runtime meant to protect running Linux systems against known exploits while teams test and roll out patches. The name is Japanese for shield, and the temporary protections it applies are called shields.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to OpenAI, the tool targets the gap between a disclosure and a fix. Testing and deploying a patch can take days or weeks, the company said, and simply blocking the affected Linux operation could take a service offline. Shirudo lets operators check whether a shield stops the exploit behavior while legitimate requests still go through, then deploy it after approval without restarting the service.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How the shields work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Shirudo is built on eBPF, a Linux technology that runs small programs at specific points inside the operating system to observe activity and apply targeted controls. The Register described these programs as sandboxed kernel plug-ins that do not get unrestricted access to system resources. OpenAI said operators can watch the effect of a proposed shield before switching it to enforcement.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI said shields are cryptographically signed and verified before they load, that the Linux eBPF verifier checks each program against safety rules, and that a Trusted Platform Module keeps a verifiable record of which protections were loaded or removed. The code is published on GitHub under the BSD 2-Clause license, with its BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"SiliconANGLE reported that Shirudo is the first effort under what the two companies call the Secure Infrastructure Project, and that it grew out of Tetragon, an open-source runtime security project from Isovalent. The Register noted that Cisco owns Isovalent, which also created the Cilium networking project.","sources":[{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/23/cisco-and-openai-launch-shirudo-an-open-source-infrastructure-shield-to-protect-against-ai-driven-cyberattacks/"},{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A Codex test against Java4Shell","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In a controlled test described by OpenAI, its Codex coding agent generated a shield that blocked an attempt to exploit Java4Shell, a recently disclosed Java flaw, against a running Elasticsearch service. OpenAI said the shield added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder and was attached to the live process, so the malicious input was rejected while Elasticsearch kept running.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/23/cisco-and-openai-launch-shirudo-an-open-source-infrastructure-shield-to-protect-against-ai-driven-cyberattacks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"SiliconANGLE, citing Cisco, described a wider workflow in which Codex, given exploit details, builds a reproducer, designs a mitigation, validates it and deploys signed shields to every affected machine. OpenAI's own announcement describes these agent controls as something the companies are still designing, and The Register reported that the companies expect a human to check every shield before it reaches production.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/23/cisco-and-openai-launch-shirudo-an-open-source-infrastructure-shield-to-protect-against-ai-driven-cyberattacks/"},{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Thomas Graf, Cisco's security chief technology officer, told SiliconANGLE that fixes can take weeks or even months, a delay he called no longer acceptable now that attackers often exploit flaws before fixes arrive. OpenAI President Greg Brockman said in the announcement that because so many teams rely on the same software, it makes sense to build these defenses in the open.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/23/cisco-and-openai-launch-shirudo-an-open-source-infrastructure-shield-to-protect-against-ai-driven-cyberattacks/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A crowded patching problem","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Register placed the launch against a surge in vulnerability reports, saying more than 100,000 software flaws were reported this year, many after AI-powered bug finders appeared. It listed other companies that sell similar compensating controls, including VMware, Palo Alto Networks, Rapid7 and Rimini Street, and observed that the project is not entirely altruistic because it could raise demand for Codex.","sources":[{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"In NeuraFeed's reading, Shirudo is an attempt to put AI on the defensive side of a race that AI bug hunting has sped up. The open license, signing and hardware-backed records address the trust question that comes with letting a model write code that runs inside the kernel. The published material so far shows one controlled demonstration, not results from large production fleets.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal is whether tested shields start shipping alongside vulnerability disclosures, a goal OpenAI named in its announcement, and whether Linux distributions or large cloud operators adopt the runtime. A technical deep dive for developers is scheduled for December 15, 2026.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Base44 to build a working app for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On the Base44 home screen, say who the app is for, what it helps them do and why it is useful. Keep the first prompt to the core idea. Add details later. item.title: UC is giving 300,000 students ChatGPT for $1.2 million
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: UC signed a one-year, $1.2 million deal with OpenAI. ChatGPT Edu and the Codex coding agent go to students, staff and faculty starting December 1. The system has about 300,000 students and 265,000 workers. Cal State renewed its OpenAI deal in July: $39 million over three years for 470,000 students. UC's IT chief said UC "played hardball" and threatened to go with Anthropic instead. Sources: Sacramento Bee, EdSource via LAist, UC Office of the President.

item.title: Anthropic now lets Claude approve code changes on its own, with no human click needed
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Claude Ship combines Code Review, which is already generally available, with two new beta agents: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. item.title: Claude claims a 47-year-old math proof no human has checked
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 23, Anthropic added a paper called "VP ≠ VNP over every field" to its public math repository, credited to an internal research version of Claude. It targets a question Leslie Valiant posed in 1979. The proof comes with Lean code that a computer can check. But the README says no human mathematician has checked the proof. It also says the result does not settle P vs NP. Sources: CASRAI, Kingy AI.

item.title: How to use Veo for free: 5 AI video clips a day in Google Flow
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Video in the Gemini app now needs a paid Google AI plan. Flow is free for adults in supported countries: open labs.google/fx/tools/flow in Chrome or Edge and sign in. item.title: Starting November 24, Wells Fargo says anything your AI agent does in your account is on you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Wells Fargo's updated online banking terms take effect November 24. They say: "Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK." Whatever an agent does is treated as if you did it yourself, with no further checks. The terms say Wells Fargo does not monitor, screen or review what AI agents do in your account. Cut an agent off? Keep proof that you revoked its access, and hand it over if the bank asks. JPMorgan, Citi and Schwab block outside AI agents from logging in for customers. Sources: Wells Fargo, American Banker, AIM Media House, Hunton Andrews Kurth.

Instead, it rewrote its online access terms so the risk of using an agent sits with the customer, and it reserved the right to limit or end agent access at any time.","sources":[{"name":"Hunton Andrews Kurth","url":"https://www.hunton.com/insights/legal/major-banks-move-to-block-or-limit-customer-directed-ai-agents"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Other banks take a harder line","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said on the bank's October 13 earnings call that it would not let outside agents, including Meta's Muse, act inside customer accounts, according to Hunton Andrews Kurth. Chase's updated Digital Services Agreement, effective January 1, 2027, says a customer who gives an agent access authorizes everything the agent does. Chief financial officer Jeremy Barnum said customers who share credentials with an external agent bear the risk, AIM Media House reported.","sources":[{"name":"AIM Media House","url":"https://aimmediahouse.com/banking/wells-fargo-just-made-customers-liable-for-their-ai-agents"},{"name":"Hunton Andrews Kurth","url":"https://www.hunton.com/insights/legal/major-banks-move-to-block-or-limit-customer-directed-ai-agents"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Citigroup said it does not permit third-party AI agents or assistants to log into customer accounts, while still allowing limited read-only access through some open banking providers. Charles Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said the firm blocks unauthorized agents, including Muse, that try to move client money 10 to 20 times a week, according to Hunton Andrews Kurth.","sources":[{"name":"Hunton Andrews Kurth","url":"https://www.hunton.com/insights/legal/major-banks-move-to-block-or-limit-customer-directed-ai-agents"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Bank of America sent customers an email warning them against sharing login details with AI tools that offer to act on their behalf, and telling them they are responsible for activity that results from such access, according to AIM Media House, which cited TechCrunch.","sources":[{"name":"AIM Media House","url":"https://aimmediahouse.com/banking/wells-fargo-just-made-customers-liable-for-their-ai-agents"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"An open legal question","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Federal Regulation E protects consumers against unauthorized electronic transfers. AIM Media House noted that when a customer has handed credentials to another party, that protection may not apply in the same way, and that no court or regulator has ruled on the question for AI agents. Hunton Andrews Kurth said guidance on authorization and liability may follow.","sources":[{"name":"AIM Media House","url":"https://aimmediahouse.com/banking/wells-fargo-just-made-customers-liable-for-their-ai-agents"},{"name":"Hunton Andrews Kurth","url":"https://www.hunton.com/insights/legal/major-banks-move-to-block-or-limit-customer-directed-ai-agents"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The bank terms show how the industry is handling agents that can log in and move money before any common rules exist. Rather than wait for regulators, banks are either shutting outside agents out or writing contracts that place the loss on the customer. For consumers, the practical effect is that a mistake by an agent with full login access may be treated as their own instruction.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Chase's new agreement takes effect on January 1, 2027, and any guidance from US regulators on whether Regulation E covers transfers made by AI agents would decide who pays when an agent gets a payment wrong.","sources":[]}]}

Open the agent and describe the task","text":"On the web, the agent lives at kimi.com/agent. In the app, Kimi's instructions are to pick K3 or K3 Swarm in the model switch above the chat box. Watch the work, then download the result","text":"While the agent runs, you can follow its reasoning, the tools it calls, the websites it visits and the intermediate steps. When it finishes you get the deliverable: a code project, Word, PDF or Markdown documents, Excel or CSV sheets, slides, charts, or a deployed web page you can preview, download or share.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Turn a report into a slide deck","text":"Turn the PDF I uploaded into a 12 slide presentation for [audience]. One idea per slide, a short title, no more than 3 bullet points each, and a final slide with the 3 main takeaways. Deliver it as an editable PPT file.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Clean up a messy spreadsheet","text":"In the Excel file I uploaded, remove duplicate rows, fix the date column so every date uses the same format, and add a summary sheet with totals by [category] and a chart of the monthly trend. Kimi describes it as long-form research with complex search, multi-step reasoning and charts, and its help center has a prompt library sorted by use: industry research, competitor analysis, due diligence, legal research, academic work, policy and personal decisions.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Research before a big purchase","text":"Research [product category] for someone who [your situation]. Compare the 5 best options on price, reliability, and what owners complain about most. End with a clear recommendation and the 3 sources you trusted most.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For heavier jobs, Kimi also lists Agent Swarm, which it says can coordinate up to 300 sub-agents and more than 4,000 tool calls, Kimi Code, a command line tool and VS Code extension for programmers, Kimi Claw, a cloud agent it says starts in under 30 seconds, and Kimi Work, a desktop agent for Mac and Windows.","sources":[{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Kimi overview","url":"https://www.kimi.ai/help/getting-started/overview"},{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Kimi overview (kimi.com)","url":"https://www.kimi.com/en/help/new-user-guide/overview"},{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Introducing Kimi Agent","url":"https://www.kimi.com/en/help/agent/agent-overview"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Kimi costs and where it falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Wikipedia, the Kimi apps are free with general rate limits, and paid plans named Moderato, Allegro, Allegretto and Vivace raise those limits and speed up agent tasks. The help pages used for this guide do not list prices, so check the membership page inside Kimi before you pay. Deep Research tasks use credits, according to Kimi's own FAQ list.","sources":[{"name":"Wikipedia: Kimi (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi_(chatbot)"},{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Deep Research","url":"https://www.kimi.com/en/help/deep-research"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Two things to know before you trust it with work data. Moonshot AI is based in Beijing, so read the privacy terms with that in mind. And Kimi K3 has faced accusations, including from the director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, that it was built by distilling Anthropic's Claude, according to Wikipedia.","sources":[{"name":"Wikipedia: Kimi (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi_(chatbot)"},{"name":"Wikipedia: Moonshot AI","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonshot_AI"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Kimi is a strong pick for long documents, slides and spreadsheet work, and its agent is generous for a free app. Like every chatbot, it can be confidently wrong, so check numbers and quotes against the source before you send anything Kimi made.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Best Lovable prompts to build an app faster (8 to copy)","dek":"Eight copy and paste prompts built on Lovable's own docs, for planning, design, login, scoped changes and bug fixes that do not waste credits.","summary":"Eight Lovable prompts based on Lovable's prompting best practices, prompt library and debugging guide. Each one asks for one change, names where it goes and says what must stay the same.","seo_title":"Best Lovable prompts: 8 to copy for building apps faster","seo_description":"8 Lovable prompts to copy: make it ask questions first, pick a design, add login, lock what must not change, report bugs and turn fixes into project rules.","answer_summary":"Good Lovable prompts ask for one change at a time, name the page or component, describe the result you want and say what must not change. For big changes, use Plan mode or ask Lovable to ask you questions before it builds.","tags":["Lovable","Prompts","Vibe coding","AI app builder","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"The best Lovable prompts are short, scoped and specific. They say what to build, where it goes and what must stay the same. This guide collects eight prompts built on Lovable's own documentation: its prompting best practices, its prompt library and its debugging guide. Fill in the [brackets], send one prompt at a time and check the result before the next one.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Why this matters: every build costs credits, and Lovable fills any gap in your prompt with its own guesses. LowCode Agency founder Jesus Vargas, in a prompting guide updated on October 16, 2026, says those guesses are often wrong. His fix is four parts in every prompt: the current state of the project, the exact page or component, the result the user should see, and what must not change.","sources":[{"name":"LowCode Agency: Lovable prompting guide","url":"https://www.lowcode.agency/blog/lovable-prompting-guide"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you are new to Lovable, start with our guide on how to use Lovable to build an app without coding. This one assumes you already have a project open.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Best Lovable prompts for planning","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Make Lovable ask you questions first","text":"I want to add [feature] to my app. Before you build anything, ask me any questions you need to fully understand what I want from this feature.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompting best practices recommend closing a prompt with a request for clarifying questions, and say this works especially well in Plan mode. The prompt library gives the same advice for large prompts: ask Lovable to check its questions first, or use Plan mode to agree on the approach before it builds.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Have Lovable rewrite your prompt","text":"Here is a prompt I plan to send you: [paste your prompt]. Rewrite it to be clearer and more specific: name the pages, the components and what must not change. Do not build anything yet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompting handbook calls this meta prompting: you ask the AI to refine your prompt before you use it. The same handbook recommends scoped edits, where you tell the AI to change only certain files or sections and leave other pages alone.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Blog: The Lovable prompting handbook","url":"https://lovable.dev/blog/2025-01-16-lovable-prompting-handbook"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"A rewrite costs one message and often saves several. A vague prompt like \"make the dashboard better\" can turn into a long chain of fixes, while a rewritten version names the cards, the chart and the table you actually want.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Three design directions before building","text":"Describe three different design directions for the hero section of [your app] before you build anything. For each one, give the style, the colors and the fonts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompt library includes a prompt that asks for three directions for the hero section before anything is built, plus ready-made style prompts for minimal, glassmorphic, bold, playful, calm and editorial looks. Its best practices page suggests picking the style early and saving your chosen keywords in the project's instructions so every later prompt uses them.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for building features","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Add login the right way","text":"Add sign up, log in and forgot password pages that match the app's current style. Require login before the dashboard. Add a Sign in with Google button next to email and password. Show clear error and success states on every form.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is based on the sign up and login prompt in Lovable's prompt library, which runs on Lovable's built-in backend. The library says each of its prompts is meant to work as a single Build mode message, and that some features need a paid plan: payments need Pro or higher, and email alerts need a paid plan.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use real words, not placeholder text. Lovable's best practices say real headlines and button labels show layout problems early, and that you should plan for logged-in and logged-out states and for empty, loading and error states.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Lock what must not change","text":"Only change the [page or component]. [The change you want]. Do not touch the login flow, the payment code or any other page. When you are done, tell me which files you changed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's best practices tell you to set boundaries: what to build, where it goes and what must stay unchanged, with \"only change the orders page\" as an example. Its debugging guide adds that guardrails for fragile areas such as authentication or payments belong in the same prompt as the task.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for fixing bugs","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Report a bug Lovable can fix","text":"On the [page name] page, [what is broken]. I expected [what should happen], but instead [what happens]. Here is the exact error: [paste error]. This worked before [your last change]. What is the root cause? Explain it in simple terms before you change any code.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's debugging guide describes a bug in four parts: what is broken, where it happens, what you expected and what happened instead. Add a screenshot for layout problems and the exact error text. Lovable reads console logs from the preview on its own, but errors on the published site have to be pasted in.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The guide says to use the Try to fix button once or twice when an error appears. Accounts get 10 free fixes, and each one comes back 24 hours after it is used. If the same error keeps returning, switch to Plan mode and find the root cause first, because repeated blind fixes tend to hide the real problem.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Test the whole flow in the browser","text":"Use browser testing to check that [the flow, for example sign up to checkout] works from start to finish. If something fails, reproduce it, fix it and test it again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompt library has prompts that ask it to use browser testing to check a flow such as checkout, and to reproduce a bug in the browser, fix it and then confirm the fix. It also includes a security review prompt that checks the login flow and whether API routes are secure.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 8: Turn the fix into a project rule","text":"We just fixed [the bug]. Summarize what went wrong, what we tried and the fix that worked, as a short rule I can add to the project instructions so this does not happen again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's handbook calls this reverse meta prompting, and its debugging guide gives the same advice: after a hard bug, ask Lovable to summarize the problem and the fix so it can go into project instructions. Instructions, previously called Knowledge, are read with every message. You set them in Project settings, then Instructions, with a limit of 10,000 characters.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Blog: The Lovable prompting handbook","url":"https://lovable.dev/blog/2025-01-16-lovable-prompting-handbook"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Instructions (Knowledge)","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/features/knowledge"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What these prompts cannot fix","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Good prompts do not remove every limit. Vargas writes that if three targeted corrections fail on the same issue, the cause may be a limit of the platform rather than the prompt. Lovable's own debugging guide suggests restoring a working state from version history, or editing an earlier message and choosing Revert and resend, then telling Lovable what you did.","sources":[{"name":"LowCode Agency: Lovable prompting guide","url":"https://www.lowcode.agency/blog/lovable-prompting-guide"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The pattern behind all eight prompts is the same: one change per message, a clear place, a clear result and a clear limit. Plan first when the change is big, and write down what worked so the next prompt starts from it. That is slower for the first ten minutes and faster for the rest of the project.","sources":[]}]}

GPTZero says its model performs best on longer texts and English prose, so a single paragraph gives a weaker signal than a full essay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Scan Google Docs with the browser extension","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero's browser extension works in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. GPTZero's Chrome page says it is free to install with a GPTZero account and comes with a monthly allowance of scans, highlighting sessions and chat messages, which paid plans raise. It can scan webpages when you ask it to, and in Google Docs it can scan automatically, color sentences by AI confidence and replay how the document was written.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero Support: Google Docs writing report","url":"https://support.gptzero.me/articles/7001890416-what-is-the-google-docs-writing-report-for-origin"},{"name":"GPTZero: Chrome extension","url":"https://gptzero.me/chrome"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. The report replays the writing process and evaluates whether the typing pattern looks human. If you only have view access, the menu asks you to request edit access. The free plan has a usage limit on writing reports.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you write your own work in Google Docs, the writing report is your best defense against a false flag: it shows the document being typed, edited and pasted over time, which a single score cannot.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the free and paid plans include","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to GPTZero's support center, the free plan includes 10,000 words a month, up to 10,000 characters per scan, the Basic AI Scan and one Advanced Scan. Essential adds Grammar Check, AI Vocabulary Check and scans up to 50,000 characters. Premium adds the full Advanced Scan, Writing Feedback, Plagiarism Check and batches of up to 50 files. Professional adds LMS integration, scans up to 150,000 characters and batches of up to 250 files.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero Support: Free and paid plans","url":"https://support.gptzero.me/articles/1272562776-what-is-the-difference-between-the-free-and-paid-for-plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero's support article does not list prices. PCWorld's review, published November 16, 2026, listed Premium at $23.99 a month, or $12.99 a month billed annually, with 300,000 words a month, and Professional at $45.99 a month, or $24.99 a month billed annually, with 500,000 words a month. PCWorld also noted that the free version may use your text for training.","sources":[{"name":"PCWorld: GPTZero review","url":"https://www.pcworld.com/article/3278225/gptzero-review.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How accurate GPTZero really is","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero says it keeps its false positive rate, human text wrongly flagged as AI, at no more than 1%, and reports 96.5% accuracy on documents that mix human and AI writing. It says its false positive rate on essays by non-native English speakers from the TOEFL exam is 1.1%. These are the company's own benchmarks. GPTZero also states that no AI detector is 100% accurate and that a result should be a conversation starter, not the final verdict.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero: AI detection technology","url":"https://gptzero.me/technology"},{"name":"GPTZero: AI accuracy benchmarking","url":"https://gptzero.me/news/ai-accuracy-benchmarking"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"PCWorld ran 50 samples in five groups. GPTZero scored all 10 pure AI samples, from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, as 100% AI, and all 10 human samples as 0% AI. The weak spot was AI text edited by a person: one such sample scored 96% human and another 98% human. Results on human text lightly edited with AI were inconsistent.","sources":[{"name":"PCWorld: GPTZero review","url":"https://www.pcworld.com/article/3278225/gptzero-review.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Older research is less kind to detectors in general. A Stanford study led by James Zou tested seven detectors, GPTZero among them, on 91 TOEFL essays and found that on average they classified 61.22% as AI generated, while they were near perfect on essays by U.S. eighth graders. The researchers also showed that asking a chatbot to rewrite text in more literary language helped it evade detection. GPTZero says it has since trained on more ESL writing.","sources":[{"name":"Stanford HAI: AI detectors biased against non-native English writers","url":"https://hai.stanford.edu/news/ai-detectors-biased-against-non-native-english-writers"},{"name":"Liang et al.: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2304.02819v3"},{"name":"GPTZero: AI accuracy benchmarking","url":"https://gptzero.me/news/ai-accuracy-benchmarking"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Early reporting raised the same worry. According to Wikipedia's summary, Futurism wrote in January 2023 that, based on the error rate it saw, teachers relying on the tool could falsely accuse nearly 20 percent of innocent students, and The Washington Post noted in August 2023 that even a small false positive rate could lead to wrongful accusations.","sources":[{"name":"Wikipedia: GPTZero","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPTZero"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"GPTZero is good at the easy cases: raw chatbot output and plainly human writing. It is weaker when a person has reworked AI text, and every detector's error rate becomes a real person once you scan a whole class. item.title: OpenAI's chief scientist wants every AI lab to agree on a shared speed limit for smarter models
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Jakub Pachocki argues most benchmarks are outdated, but perplexity, a score for how well a model predicts the next token, still tracks progress. Lower means better predictions. GPT-4 scored about 0.91 on OpenAI's measure. Below 0.8, the post says, models showed transformative skills in cybersecurity and math. Labs would agree not to cross a shared limit until monitoring catches up. Sam Altman called the post the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while. Sources: TechCrunch, Datastudios.

Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average, and a lower score means better predictions. TechCrunch reported that the post includes a chart showing how the perplexity of OpenAI's models has fallen since GPT-3.5.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Datastudios, the figures are log-perplexity scores measured on a held-out dataset drawn from OpenAI's internal codebase. GPT-3.5 sat at roughly 0.99 and GPT-4 at roughly 0.91. Pachocki wrote that GPT-4 was able to use chain-of-thought reasoning productively at that level, and that once OpenAI's models reached losses below 0.8, the company saw transformative capabilities emerge in fields such as cybersecurity and mathematics.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"},{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Datastudios reported that the post also cites an unnamed OpenAI model at about 0.76, linked to strong results on open math problems, and expects further capability jumps somewhere around 0.68 to 0.7. The post does not say which model reached 0.76 or whether the lower range would serve as a limit.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the proposal asks of AI labs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pachocki suggests that perplexity could act as a shared benchmark for general intelligence, which companies could use to set common limits. Under the idea, developers would commit not to go past an agreed threshold until their ability to understand and monitor AI behavior reaches a concrete milestone, TechCrunch reported.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Datastudios described the plan in three layers: shared norms for evaluating and red-teaming frontier models before first use, along with transparency standards; commitments not to cross common limits defined by perplexity and other measures until a monitoring milestone is met, with a successor to chain-of-thought monitors given as an example; and a framework for setting later limits. The post names no partner companies and no date for a first limit, and it announces no change to ChatGPT, Codex or the API, according to Datastudios.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The post also lists open problems, Datastudios reported. Labs train on different datasets, perplexity does not map directly onto real tasks, gains from chain-of-thought reasoning do not lower perplexity, and nobody knows where the loss floor lies. OpenAI said it is publishing its own numbers as a first step, while acknowledging that this gives competitors a clearer view of its progress.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The wider push for limits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The proposal arrives as calls for restraint grow inside the industry. TechCrunch noted that Anthropic's IPO filing warned the technology could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society, and that Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei has published a plan to pace the frontier, calling for common safety standards and limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress. Altman and Elon Musk reportedly endorsed that plan.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The notable part is less the idea of limits than the choice of a single number to define them. A shared metric would let rival labs check one another, but only if they agree on the dataset it is measured on, a problem the post itself raises. By publishing its own scores first, OpenAI is betting that openness will pull competitors into the same frame.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The test is whether Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI or Meta publish comparable perplexity figures or sign on to a common threshold. Without that, the proposal remains one company's yardstick.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to delete your Meta AI chats for good
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the Meta AI app, tap Menu at the top left, then Settings at the bottom left. Under App settings, tap Data & privacy, then Manage your information. Confirm with Delete all. Your chats, prompts and media leave the History and Media sections. On meta.ai, click your profile picture, then Settings and the same path. item.title: AI godfather Yann LeCun says Anthropic's Dario Amodei hypes AI dangers so he can stay in control
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 22, LeCun answered an X post about Amodei's remarks to a US congressional hearing. He wrote that Amodei has hyped the dangers since GPT-2 so that open models would be made illegal and he would stay in control. Yann LeCun, founder of AMI Labs. LeCun compared it to the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic to keep control of the dogma. He called it "a new form of medieval obscurantism" and said Amodei left OpenAI because he "wasn't going to have control." Sources: OfficeChai, The Open Press, NewsBytes.

Write down what the app does","text":"Before you type anything into Replit, list the features and the steps a user takes. Publish it","text":"Click Publish in the top right of the Project Editor. For bugs, it says to paste the exact error message, the file names, what you were trying to do and what you already tried.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Prompting guide","url":"https://docs.replit.com/getting-started/quickstarts/build-with-ai"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The first version","text":"Build a simple web app where [who] can [main task].
Features:
- [feature 1]
- [feature 2]
- [feature 3]
Store [data] in a database. Use a clean, simple design. Start with the smallest version that works, and tell me how to test it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Plan only","text":"/plan I want to add [feature] to this app. Compare two ways to do it, list the files you would change, and do not write any code yet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Fix a bug","text":"When I [action] on the [page name] page, I get this error: [paste the exact error]. I expected [what should happen]. I already tried [what you tried]. Find the cause and fix only that.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Checkpoints: your undo button","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agent creates checkpoints on its own, for example after a feature is finished and before it fixes a serious error. A checkpoint captures the project files and packages, the AI conversation, environment and publishing settings, and database contents. To go back, open the Agent tab, find the checkpoint and select Rollback to here, then confirm.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Checkpoints and rollbacks","url":"https://docs.replit.com/references/version-control/checkpoints-and-rollbacks"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Two details matter. Your development database is not restored by default: select Database under Additional rollback options to include it. And a rollback never restores the production database of a published app; Replit points to a point in time restore for that. If you make new changes after rolling back, the later checkpoints become a separate branch you cannot roll forward to.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Checkpoints and rollbacks","url":"https://docs.replit.com/references/version-control/checkpoints-and-rollbacks"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Replit Agent costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agent has three modes. Free Mode covers everyday work at no extra cost within your plan's allowance; on Core and Pro the allowance resets every five hours and also has a weekly limit, and you can check it under Settings, then Usage. Power is a paid mid tier mode and Max a paid top tier mode with the strongest models. When a request needs more than Free Mode, Agent explains why and asks first, and after a one time paid step it returns to Free Mode.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Agent overview","url":"https://docs.replit.com/references/agent/overview"},{"name":"Replit Docs: Free Mode","url":"https://docs.replit.com/help/free-agent-mode"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Paid work is priced by effort, so a small fix costs less than a whole feature. Each request produces one checkpoint, with no charges in between. Planning in Power or Max is billed like any other request, even when no code changes. You can see the cost of each checkpoint in the Agent tab by hovering over the usage icon, and a full breakdown at replit.com/usage, which can lag by up to 30 minutes.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Pricing and plans","url":"https://docs.replit.com/help/pricing-and-plans"},{"name":"Replit Docs: Agent billing","url":"https://docs.replit.com/billing/ai-billing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Replit's help center lists three plans for individuals. Starter is free, with a daily AI allowance, limited monthly cloud credits and one published app. Core costs $204 a year on annual billing and includes $20 in monthly credits, unlimited published apps and up to 5 collaborators. Pro costs $100 a month and adds more Free Mode usage, up to 15 builders and credits that roll over for two months. Credits also pay for published apps, storage and databases.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Pricing and plans","url":"https://docs.replit.com/help/pricing-and-plans"},{"name":"Replit Docs: Agent billing","url":"https://docs.replit.com/billing/ai-billing"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Set a budget before you use Power or Max. On the Billing page in Settings you can add usage alerts at spending thresholds and budget limits that act as hard caps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Replit Agent falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Independent testers like the speed but warn about cost and depth. An All About Cookies reviewer who built a legal case management app from a 23 page spec ran through the free plan's allowance in about 21 minutes, then used up a month of Core credits and was still an estimated 10 to 15 percent from a deployable app. A DEV Community review found that Agent's self testing catches obvious bugs but lets architecture problems through, and that custom CI/CD, strict Git workflows and hosting outside Replit add friction.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: Replit review","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/replit-review"},{"name":"DEV Community: Replit Agent review 2026","url":"https://dev.to/jovan_chan_9500711396d4e6/replit-agent-review-2026-from-idea-to-deployed-app-but-read-the-credit-bill-first-4cma"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Replit Agent is good at getting a simple idea to a live link fast, especially if you do not code. It is weaker at large, complex apps, where every round of fixes costs money and the structure of the code matters. Start small, plan first, keep each request narrow, and watch the usage page. If the project grows, expect to read the code yourself or bring in someone who can.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Kling vs Seedance: which AI video model to use, and what each one costs
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Kling 4.0 makes clips of 3 to 30 seconds in one pass, with up to 10 keyframes. Its Omni Reference takes up to 15 assets: images, videos, subjects and voices. Seedance 2.0 takes text plus up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips in one request. Sources: Kling AI: Kling 3.0 credit cost guide, Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide, Kling AI: Kling 4.0, Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0 to all users, ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch, Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0, Dreamina: Seedance 2.0 Lite.

Seedance is the better pick when you want to throw a pile of references at the model, including a voice or a piece of music, and get the sound back with the picture.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"},{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Kling vs Seedance at a glance","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Clip length: Kling says Kling 4.0 generates natively from 3 to 30 seconds in a single pass, and that video extension forward or backward will reach up to 2 minutes in total. Kling's older VIDEO 3.0 model runs from 3 to 15 seconds. Seedance 2.0 returns up to 15 seconds of multi-shot video, according to ByteDance's launch post.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"},{"name":"Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide","url":"https://kling.ai/quickstart/klingai-video-3-model-user-guide"},{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"References: Kling 4.0's Omni Reference accepts up to 15 assets combined. Kling's FAQ breaks that down as up to 10 images, up to 5 reference videos with a combined length of up to 30 seconds, and up to 7 subject elements, and it also takes voices. You can set up to 10 keyframes. Seedance 2.0 takes text plus up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips in one generation. Dreamina says each video or audio reference can be up to 15 seconds long.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"},{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"},{"name":"Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/resource/how-to-use-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Sound: Seedance 2.0 makes the audio together with the video. ByteDance describes dual channel stereo with separate tracks for music, ambience, effects and character voices. Kling's VIDEO 3.0 also has Native Audio, which covers dialogue, lip sync, ambience and sound effects, and its guide lists speech in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Spanish, with dialects and accents. Its page marks native 4K, 1080p and 10 bit HDR output as coming soon. Dreamina says Seedance 2.0 videos download at 1080p.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"},{"name":"Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0 to all users","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/kling-ai-opens-kling-40-to-all-users-d9dc6422"},{"name":"Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/resource/how-to-use-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Free credits and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kling sells credits through monthly plans. Its credit guide, dated July 28, 2026, lists a free Basic plan with no monthly credits and output that is not for commercial use. The Standard plan, listed from $6.99 a month, comes with 660 credits, which Kling says is about 33 videos at 720p, and adds 1080p, watermark removal and commercial use. Pro comes with 3,000 credits, Premier with 8,000 and Ultra with 26,000. Native 4K on VIDEO 3.0 costs 30 credits a second.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 3.0 credit cost guide","url":"https://kling.ai/blog/kling-video-3-0-credit-cost-guide"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kling had not announced pricing for Kling 4.0 when it launched, according to Let's Data Science, so check the credit cost shown in the app before you generate with it.","sources":[{"name":"Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0 to all users","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/kling-ai-opens-kling-40-to-all-users-d9dc6422"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Dreamina says you can start Seedance with no credit card. It also offers a lighter model, listed as Seedance 2.0 Lite on one page and Seedance 2.0 mini in its menus, which it describes as faster and cheaper to run and free to try with trial credits. Dreamina's menus also list a newer Seedance 2.5.","sources":[{"name":"Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/resource/how-to-use-seedance-2-0"},{"name":"Dreamina: Seedance 2.0 Lite","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/seedance/seedance-2-0-lite"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Neither one is truly free for regular use. On Kling, the free plan gives you an account but no monthly credits. On Dreamina, trial credits are enough to test a few ideas. If you only need a handful of clips, start on Seedance Lite; if you plan to generate every week, compare Kling's monthly credits with the cost per clip that Dreamina shows you before you pay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Which one to pick","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. You need a clip longer than 15 seconds","text":"Use Kling 4.0. It is the only one of the two that generates up to 30 seconds in one pass, so you avoid stitching two clips that do not quite match.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. You want to control exactly where the shot goes","text":"Use Kling 4.0 and set keyframes. Up to 10 of them let you pin the frames the video has to pass through.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. You have a voice, a song or a sound to match","text":"Use Seedance 2.0. Upload the audio clip next to your images and refer to each file in the prompt by name with an @ sign, the way Dreamina's guide shows (@AssetName).","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. You just want to try AI video today","text":"Open Dreamina and pick the Lite or mini model. It runs on trial credits, and the steps are the same as for the full model.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts to test both on the same shot","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The fairest test is one prompt in both tools at the same length. Keep it to one subject, one camera move and one sound, so you can see which model handles the basics better before you spend credits on a long scene.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: One subject, one camera move","text":"A slow push-in on [subject] in [place] at [time of day], soft light from the left. At the third second, [subject] turns and looks at the camera. Quiet ambient sound of [place].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A product from one photo","text":"[Product] sits on a wooden kitchen counter in morning light. The camera circles slowly to the left. Steam rises from a cup beside it. Soft acoustic guitar music.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A short line of dialogue","text":"Medium shot of [person] standing on a rainy street at night. They look up, then say in a calm voice: \"[one short line]\". Sound of rain and distant traffic.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where each one falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"ByteDance is unusually frank about Seedance 2.0. Its launch post says the model is still far from perfect: detail stability, realism and natural motion need work, keeping several subjects consistent is hard, text inside the video is not always accurate, and the audio can occasionally distort.","sources":[{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Using a real person's face as a Seedance reference requires identity verification or prior legal authorization, according to ByteDance. If an upload is rejected, check whether it shows a real face before you rewrite the prompt.","sources":[{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Kling's weak spot is cost and paperwork. Every re-roll spends credits, commercial use and watermark removal sit behind a paid plan, and some of Kling 4.0's headline features, such as two minute extension and 4K HDR, were still listed as coming when this guide was written. The quality claims for both models come from the companies themselves, so a ten minute test with your own prompt is worth more than any spec sheet.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Grok Imagine for AI images and video
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Go to grok.com/imagine or open the Grok app on iPhone or Android. For pictures, pick Quality Mode. That is where the new Image 2.0 model runs. A clip runs 1 to 15 seconds, 8 by default, at 480p, 720p or 1080p. Sound is on by default. Turning a photo into a video keeps the photo's shape. Sources: xAI Docs: Image and Video Overview, xAI Docs: Video Generation, xAI Docs: Video Overview, Tech Insider: How to use Grok Imagine Image 2.0, Magnific: Grok Imagine, how to use, features, prompts.

Warm light in the windows, light rain on the glass, steam rising from a cup on the counter. Quiet street sounds and soft rain.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A product shot","text":"Minimal product video of a [product] turning slowly on a white table in a bright studio. Keep the people, their faces, their clothes and the buildings exactly the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For words inside an image, Tech Insider recommends putting the exact text in quotation marks and keeping it short, such as a headline and one line.","sources":[{"name":"Tech Insider: How to use Grok Imagine Image 2.0","url":"https://tech-insider.org/how-to-use-grok-imagine-image-2-2026/"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A poster with readable text","text":"A clean coffee poster on a cream background with a single cup in the center. item.title: Players caught AI-made music hidden in The Binding of Isaac's new update
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The November 19 update added a GTA-themed daily run called Crime Mode. A Reddit user checked its music files and found Suno metadata in them. The Steam page had no AI disclosure. Creator Edmund McMillen said he had no idea and was getting it removed. Publisher Nicalis patched the files out on PC. Recent Steam reviews: 8% positive, rated Overwhelmingly Negative. Sources: GamesRadar+, PC Gamer, ShiftDelete.Net, Power Up Gaming, Steam.

item.title: How to use Descript: edit your video by deleting words from the transcript
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Descript transcribes your file and links the text to the media. Select words and press Delete to cut them from both. Changed your mind? Right click the edit and choose Restore removed media. In the AI Tools panel, choose Remove filler words to find every um and uh in the script.
