The free plan includes basic editing but no AI credits, and paid plans start at $24.99 a month for 500 credits.","seo_title":"How to use Captions AI: AI Edit, captions and plans","seo_description":"How to use Captions AI step by step: run AI Edit, add captions in about 100 languages, dub videos, export, and see what the free and paid plans include.","answer_summary":"Open the Captions app, keep Edit selected on Home, add your clip, pick a style and an effort level, and tap Create project. Captions and basic edits work on the free plan, but AI features such as AI Edit, eye contact and caption styles need a paid plan to export.","tags":["Captions","Captions AI","AI video editing","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Captions is an AI video editor built by Mirage, a New York AI research company, and it runs on iPhone, Android and the web at captions.ai, according to its help center. If you want to know how to use Captions AI, the short version: record or import a talking video, let AI Edit cut it, check the captions, then export. Basic editing is free. The AI parts are not.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: AI Edit","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/project/ai-edit"},{"name":"Captions: Pricing","url":"https://captions.ai/pricing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Captions works best for one person talking to the camera. Its own docs recommend a single speaker, say captions work best on clips of 60 to 90 seconds, and suggest keeping imported footage under three minutes for AI Edit.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: AI Edit","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/project/ai-edit"},{"name":"Captions Help: Add captions","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/captions/add-captions"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Captions AI Edit on your phone","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Update the app","text":"AI Edit is rolling out on iOS, according to the help center. If you do not see it, update the app first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Start an Edit project","text":"On the Home screen, keep Edit selected and add your media. Pick a style, such as Cozy, Vox-Style or Tour, and if you want, type a short description of the edit you have in mind. Tap Continue.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Choose the options","text":"Pick a model, then review Inputs and options: the aspect ratio, a Voiceover only toggle, and the output shape, Portrait 9:16 or Landscape 16:9. Set the effort level: Quick is the default, then Standard, Advanced and Ultra. Ultra puts the result ahead of speed and cost.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Check the credit estimate and create","text":"Before you start, Captions shows an estimated range of credits. The help center says you never pay more than the top of that range, and shows the real usage after each result. Tap Create project.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Decide on the model and effort before you tap Create project. The docs say you cannot change the model after a project starts, or the effort after it is created.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Fix things by hand when you can","text":"Manual edits on the timeline use no credits. Follow up edits you ask for in the chat do use credits, so small trims are cheaper to make yourself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Add captions and translations","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"To caption a video on iPhone, import or record it, choose the spoken language, then choose No Translation or a target language, according to the help center. The help page lists about 100 languages, plus a Multiple Languages option. You can also add a caption by hand: tap Add, type it, then Apply.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: Add captions","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/captions/add-captions"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There are length limits. Same language captions work on videos up to 10 minutes on iOS and the web and 5 minutes on Android. Captions in another language and dubbing are limited to 5 minutes on every platform. On the web, the help center says changing the caption style costs extra credits.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: Add captions","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/captions/add-captions"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Dubbing, eye contact and AI Twin","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Dubbing replaces the audio with another language, and Lipdub also re-animates the speaker's lips, according to Captions. It lists more than 30 dubbing languages, including Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Japanese and Portuguese, and says Lipdub clones your voice. Captions says you can start dubbing for free, while Lipdub is a premium feature.","sources":[{"name":"Captions: AI Dubbing","url":"https://captions.ai/features/ai-dubbing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Eye Contact is a tool in the app's editing panel that corrects your gaze after recording, for talking head footage. AI Twin creates an avatar of you from a short recording where you read a script; Captions lists it as a Max plan feature and recommends recording in a quiet room.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: Export","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/settings/export.md"},{"name":"Captions: AI Twin","url":"https://captions.ai/features/create-ai-twin"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Captions AI plans and credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan includes basic tools such as trim, transitions, zoom and sound effects, one caption template and no AI credits, according to the pricing page. Max costs $24.99 a month with 500 credits. Frontier costs $69.99 a month with 1,400 credits, and Frontier 2x and 4x cost $139.99 and $279.99 for 2,800 and 5,600 credits. Captions says these prices reflect its iOS plans. An independent review by eesel AI lists the same prices and credit amounts.","sources":[{"name":"Captions: Pricing","url":"https://captions.ai/pricing"},{"name":"eesel AI: Captions AI features, pricing and limitations","url":"https://www.eesel.ai/blog/captions-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Unused credits roll over to the next month, up to three times your monthly allowance, according to the credits page. Individual top ups are not available on standard plans, and canceling forfeits the remaining credits at the end of the period.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: Credits","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/troubleshooting/credits.md"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Export","text":"Tap Export, choose your settings and tap Export again. Advanced options include resolution, frame rate, bitrate and a separate SRT caption file. Basic manual edits export free, but the help center says AI features such as AI Edit, caption styles, eye contact correction and background music need a paid subscription, and the app asks for one when you export.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Captions is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Try your edit on the free plan before you pay. You only find out at export that a feature you used needs a subscription, so it is worth knowing which tools are AI features first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Captions is built for short videos of one person talking. The help center itself steers you toward clips of a minute or two, and the five minute caps on translation and dubbing rule it out for long interviews. The eesel AI review also points to a learning curve and to app store complaints about lag, captions going out of sync after edits and crashes at export. Credits make the monthly cost hard to predict if you lean on chat edits and high effort levels, so start with Quick and do small fixes by hand.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Perplexity prompts: 7 to copy for faster research","dek":"Seven copy and paste prompts built on Perplexity's own help center tips, for quick answers, comparisons, Deep Research reports and files.","summary":"Seven Perplexity prompts based on the tips in Perplexity's help center. Each one adds context, asks for one thing and names the format, and three of them use Deep Research or file creation, which depend on your plan.","seo_title":"Perplexity prompts: 7 to copy and paste for faster research","seo_description":"7 Perplexity prompts to copy: ask with context, compare options, run Deep Research, analyze your own file and turn the results into a spreadsheet or deck.","answer_summary":"Good Perplexity prompts state one clear goal, add a line of context, use the keywords that matter and name the format (a table, bullet points or steps). For long reports, use Deep Research from the plus (+) menu, which Perplexity includes on Pro, Max and Enterprise plans.","tags":["Perplexity","Prompts","AI search","Deep Research","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"These Perplexity prompts come from Perplexity's own help center, which lists the habits that get better answers: say what you want, give context, ask for one thing at a time and name the format. Below are seven prompts built on those tips, with [brackets] where your details go. Paste one in, fill the brackets, and you get a cited answer instead of a pile of links.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"},{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Practical tips for using Perplexity","url":"https://intercom.help/perplexity-ai/en/articles/10352971-how-can-i-use-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity's help center describes a good prompt as five parts: an instruction, context, the input, keywords that matter, and the output format you want. You do not need all five every time, but most weak answers miss at least two of them. The help center gives \"Cars.\" as an example of a search that is too vague to be useful.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Practical tips for using Perplexity","url":"https://intercom.help/perplexity-ai/en/articles/10352971-how-can-i-use-perplexity"},{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts for everyday research","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The question with context","text":"I'm a [who you are] in [where you live]. [Your question, as one clear sentence]. Give me the answer as [a table / bullet points / a step by step guide].","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"This is the base pattern, and every other prompt here is a version of it. Perplexity's own example is a first-time homebuyer in the US asking which federal programs can help. The context line changes the sources it picks, and the format line saves you from reformatting the answer yourself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Compare two options","text":"Compare the pros and cons of [option A] vs. [option B] for [your situation]. Put the result in a table with one row per point, and note which sources disagree.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Add the keywords that actually decide the answer. The help center's example is \"best noise-canceling headphones under $200 for commuting\": the price and the use case do more work than the word headphones.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Arguments for and against","text":"Summarize the main arguments for and against [idea or decision], with supporting data. Keep each side to five points and link the source for every number.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity's help center uses a four-day work week as its example for this one. It works for anything people argue about: a policy, a purchase, a career move. Asking for a fixed number of points per side keeps the answer balanced and short enough to read.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts for Deep Research","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Deep Research reads many sources and writes a detailed report. According to Perplexity's help center, it is included on Perplexity Pro, Perplexity Max, Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max. To start it, open the plus (+) menu in the search bar and pick Deep Research; on the web you can also type / in the search bar. Perplexity notes the menu can look different depending on the platform.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A full report on one question","text":"Research [topic] and [what you want it to suggest or explain], including [the detail you care about most, for example cost comparisons].","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Be clear about what you want to learn before you hit enter. Perplexity's sample is \"the environmental impact of fast fashion and sustainable alternatives, including cost comparisons\". The help center contrasts it with \"Tell me about fashion\", which gives Deep Research nothing to aim at.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Narrow it down","text":"Now focus on [one part of the report]. What does the evidence say, and where is it weak?","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start broad, then narrow with follow-ups in the same thread, as the help center recommends. Its example is a report on remote work trends in the United States since 2020, followed by \"Now focus on the impact on employee productivity.\" One big question and two short follow-ups usually beat one giant prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Your file plus the web","text":"Based on the attached [report, contract or spreadsheet] and the latest [market data or news], what's the outlook for [company, product or plan]? Separate what comes from my file and what comes from the web.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity's help center says you can upload your own files and ask Deep Research to analyze them next to web sources, using an attached financial report as its example. The last sentence of the prompt above is our addition: it makes it easier to see which claims came from your document.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts that make a file","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Turn research into a document, deck or sheet","text":"Build a spreadsheet comparing the top [5] [tools or products] by [price], [features] and [user ratings].","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Depending on your plan, Perplexity can create documents, slide decks and spreadsheets, and the help center says documents include citations. Say the file type plainly, for example \"Create a Word document\", \"Build a slide deck\" or \"Make a spreadsheet\", and describe the structure, such as a 10-slide presentation with sections on budget, channels and key metrics. Documents export as .pdf or .docx, presentations as .pptx and spreadsheets as .xlsx.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Fix the file with short follow-ups instead of rewriting the prompt. The help center's examples are \"Add a conclusion slide\" and \"Make the executive summary shorter.\" You can also run a search first and then ask Perplexity to turn the results into a document or deck in the same session, if your plan includes file creation.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to write your own Perplexity prompts","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Start with one clear goal","text":"Write the question you would ask an expert, not a search keyword. Asking for the current inflation rate in the US works; \"inflation\" makes Perplexity guess.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add who you are and why you ask","text":"One sentence of background is enough. Perplexity's tips and the University of Florida Business Library's guide both point out that context and follow-up questions are what turn a generic answer into a useful one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Ask for one thing and name the format","text":"A table, bullet points or a step by step guide. If you need three things, ask three times in the same thread.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Test and tweak","text":"Perplexity's help center tells users to test prompts and adjust them. If the answer misses, change one part of the prompt (the context, the keywords or the format), not all of it at once.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Perplexity falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity is only as good as the question. Vague prompts get vague answers, and the help center says so with examples like \"Cars.\" and \"Write something for me.\" Usage limits depend on your plan, the help center lists Deep Research only for Pro, Max and Enterprise plans, file creation also depends on the plan, and every regenerated or edited image counts as a new generation toward your image limit. The citations make it easy to check an answer, so open at least one source for any number you plan to reuse.","sources":[]}]}
